To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
during liver regeneration the levels of the individual deoxynucleoside tri- and diphosphates increase in parallel with the increase in DNA synthesis.
the deoxyriboside triphospates (dNTP) increase during liver regeneration and that the increase coincides with the increase in DNA synthesis.
during liver regeneration the levels of the four deoxyribonucletide triphosphatases increase and reach maxima at the peak of DNA replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the intracellular pools of dATP and dCTP during liver regeneration.
the analysis of the intracellular pools of the deoxyribosylated nucleotides during liver regeneration in the rat.
the regulation of deoxyribnucleoside triplphosphate pools during liver regeneration and with the possible role of the deoxyribnuleoside triphos-phate pools in controlling DNA replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deoxyribosynthetic capacity of the regenerating rat liver is increased in parallel with the rate of DNA replication, which in turn is dependent on the intracellular levels of dATP and dTTP.
the increase in deoxyribonucletide pool size is a consequence of the increase in DNA synthesis and is probably not the cause of the increased rate of DNA synthesis during liver regeneration.
the increase of the intracellular levels of deoxy ribonucleosides during liver regeneration is a consequence of the increased rate of DNA synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intracellular deoxyribonucletide pool is regulated in a complex manner by the activity of ribonucleotide reduc tase.

during liver regeneration the deoxyribnucleoside tripphosphate pools increase in the same way as the DNA synthesis, but that this process is regulated by a feedback control of the ribonucleotide reduction.

the intracellular levels of the deoxyribosylated nucleotides increase during liver regeneration in parallel with the rate of DNA biosynthesis, and that ribonucleotide reduction is induced in the regenerating liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intracellular levels of deoxy ribonucleotides are not limiting in vivo for DNA synthesis.
the intracellular deoxyribonucloetide pools are not in equilibrium during liver regeneration.
the deoxyriboside triphophate pool is a limiting factor for DNA synthesis.
